Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

for conjunction

because (giving the reason)

also you see, for (explaining), you see (parenthetical)

classical

Quint. 1.11.3: nam frequēns imitātiō trānsit in mōrēs

nam

conjunction, first in its clause, with the indicative

Gives the reason or the explanation of what has just been said, as a new sentence. Only where the clause really explains: not as glue, and not after a colon.

Other words

  • enim — for, you see

    conjunction, second in its clause · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.9.1: jam diū ignōrō quid agās; nihil enim scrībis; Varr. RR 2.1.2: nēmō enim omnia potest scīre; Traupman 410

    The same, lighter, and the commoner in talk; it stands after the first word. Neque enim, for … not.

  • etenim (namque) — for indeed

    conjunction, first in its clause · also used · classical · Verg. A. 1.327–328: namque haud tibi vultus mortālis

    A stronger “for”, mostly in formal prose and poetry.

  • quippe — for in fact, since of course

    particle: opens its clause; quippe quī, since he · also used · classical · Hor. S. 1.2.4: quippe benignus erat (Lewis & Short); Ov. Met. 2.852: quippe color nivis est (Lewis & Short); Cic. Rosc. Am. 52: quippe quī nē in oppidum quidem, nisi perrārō, venīret (Lewis & Short)

    A particle of assurance, “to be sure, of course”, which brings in the explanation; often ironical: quippe vetor fātīs (Verg. A. 1.39). As a plain “for, because” not in Cicero or Caesar (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • nam frequēns imitātiō trānsit in mōrēs

    for frequent imitation turns into characterQuint. 1.11.3

  • nam mihi ante oculōs diēs noctēsque versāris

    for you are before my eyes day and nightCic. Fam. 14.2.3

  • jam diū ignōrō quid agās; nihil enim scrībis

    I haven’t known for a long time how you are, for you never writeCic. Fam. 7.9.1

  • nēmō enim omnia potest scīre

    for nobody can know everythingVarr. RR 2.1.2

  • quis enim scrūtātus est?

    for who has looked?Tac. Germ. 5.3

  • quippe color nivis est

    for its colour is that of snowOv. Met. 2.852 (Lewis & Short)

See also because, since, of course.
